requirement:
Habeas MUST locate its per-user configuration at
`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/habeas/config.toml` on Unix when XDG_CONFIG_HOME is an absolute,
nonempty path, otherwise at `$HOME/.config/habeas/config.toml`. On Windows it MUST
use `%APPDATA%/habeas/config.toml`. `HOME` and `APPDATA` MUST likewise be
absolute, nonempty paths to be used. If no usable base directory can be
determined, an operation requiring user configuration MUST fail with an
explanatory diagnostic naming the variable.

The same user configuration MUST be usable across projects. Its location MUST
NOT be selected relative to the current project or changed by project settings.
User-local preferences for a project MAY remain in the user configuration;
workspace settings MUST use `habeas.toml` under
{cite}`requirements.configuration.workspace_location`.
rationale:
**Judgment: the requirement is met. The implementation is complete and marked, and the tests cover the behaviour.**

**Implementation (src/config.rs)**
- `ConfigPlatform::current()` (line 239) selects Windows or Unix with `cfg!(windows)`.
- `user_config_path()` (line 611) passes the real environment lookup, `std::env::var_os`, to `user_config_path_from()`.
- `user_config_path_from()` (lines 616–629) does what the requirement says:
  - On Unix it uses `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` only if it is absolute and nonempty. Otherwise it uses `$HOME/.config`. In both cases it appends `habeas/config.toml`.
  - On Windows it uses `%APPDATA%/habeas/config.toml`.
  - `HOME` and `APPDATA` go through `required_directory`, so they must also be absolute and nonempty.
- `absolute_directory` (lines 652–658) rejects empty and relative values. An empty `PathBuf` is not absolute.
- `required_directory` (lines 660–672) returns an `io::Error` whose message names the variable: "cannot determine Habeas directory: {name} must be an absolute, nonempty path".
- Callers propagate that error with `?`, for example `resolve_authoring` (line 888) via `user_config_path()?`. An operation that needs user configuration therefore fails with the diagnostic.
- The path depends only on environment variables. It does not use the project root or any workspace setting, so it is the same across projects and cannot be changed by project settings. A search for `config.toml` and `HOME` in `src` found no other code that computes the user path.
- Workspace settings are handled separately under `habeas.toml`. That belongs to `workspace_location`, which I did not reassess.
- All implementing helpers carry `{impl}` markers. `state_location` shares `absolute_directory`, `required_directory` and `ConfigPlatform::current`, and those markers are present for both requirements. I found no unmarked implementing code and no unspecified behaviour.

**Tests (tests/configuration.rs)**
- `locations_use_absolute_xdg_values_and_platform_fallbacks` covers:
  - a valid absolute `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`;
  - an empty or relative XDG value falling back to `$HOME/.config`;
  - the Windows `APPDATA` path;
  - an error when no variables are set.
- `base_directories_must_be_absolute_and_nonempty` covers:
  - an empty or relative `HOME` (Unix) or `APPDATA` (Windows) producing an error that names the variable;
  - a relative XDG value falling back to an absolute `HOME`.
- The remaining obligations (independence from the project, and the location not being changed by project settings) hold structurally, because the function reads nothing but environment variables. A dedicated negative test would add little.
- Several CLI test fixtures set `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`/`APPDATA` explicitly, which exercises the real lookup path end to end.

I found no gaps.

text: :::{req} user_location
Habeas MUST locate its per-user configuration at
`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/habeas/config.toml` on Unix when XDG_CONFIG_HOME is an absolute,
nonempty path, otherwise at `$HOME/.config/habeas/config.toml`. On Windows it MUST
use `%APPDATA%/habeas/config.toml`. `HOME` and `APPDATA` MUST likewise be
absolute, nonempty paths to be used. If no usable base directory can be
determined, an operation requiring user configuration MUST fail with an
explanatory diagnostic naming the variable.
The same user configuration MUST be usable across projects. Its location MUST
NOT be selected relative to the current project or changed by project settings.
User-local preferences for a project MAY remain in the user configuration;
workspace settings MUST use `habeas.toml` under
{cite}`requirements.configuration.workspace_location`.
:::{req} workspace_location
Habeas MUST search from its invocation directory upward for the nearest enclosing
`habeas.toml`. It MUST use that file alone, without merging ancestor workspace
files. A library operation given a project root MUST search from that root unless
its current directory is inside the project, in which case it MUST start there.
The directory containing the selected file defines the base for its relative
paths; it does not replace the Cargo and mdBook project root. A missing file MUST
mean absent workspace settings. Discovery MUST report unreadable candidate files
rather than silently selecting an ancestor. Loading MUST NOT create the file.
